issues.legal_issue: A tenant parts with possession of leased premises when a third party regularly uses a major portion of them and the tenant does not retain effective exclusive control, even if no rent-paying subletting is proved.
material_facts: A social club regularly used the premises to assemble and play games, and its name board was displayed there.
The club had its registered office at the premises and was subject to statutory requirements relating to records, inspections and service of documents there.
The tenant retained no demonstrated practice of locking the premises and denying the club members entry, though he said he conducted business in a small portion.
The lower courts found no subletting for rent, but the appellate court found that possession had been parted with.
issues.conclusion: The tenant had parted with possession of a major portion of the premises to the club, making him liable for eviction under Section 13(1)(e) of the Rajasthan Premises (Control of Rent and Eviction) Act, 1950; proof of rent-paying subletting was unnecessary.
issues.legal_principle: Section 13(1)(e) independently covers assigning, subletting, or otherwise parting with possession of all or any part of the premises without the landlord’s permission; consequently, absence of proof of rent or a conventional sublease does not defeat eviction if possession was otherwise parted with. The club’s registered office and the Companies Act, 1956, including Section 146 and the related requirements concerning company records, inspection and service, supported the inference that it had possession. Smt. Rajbir Kaur v. M/s. S. Chokesiri & Co. was distinguished because it concerned occupants shown to be licensees and a different rent statute whose provision did not include the phrase “otherwise parting with the possession.”

rule.if: tenant_eviction_case and third_party_regularly_uses_major_portion and tenant_does_not_exercise_exclusive_control and third_party_has_registered_office_there and landlord_permission_not_shown

predicates.tenant_eviction_case: The proceeding seeks eviction of a tenant from leased premises.
predicates.third_party_regularly_uses_major_portion: A third party regularly uses a major portion of the premises.
predicates.tenant_does_not_exercise_exclusive_contr: The tenant does not demonstrate that the tenant keeps the premises under exclusive control by excluding the third party.
predicates.third_party_has_registered_office_there: The third party maintains its registered office at the premises, with the resulting need to use them for its official functions.
predicates.landlord_permission_not_shown: The tenant has not shown that the landlord permitted the transfer of possession.

issues.definition: When an eviction case involves regular third-party use of a major portion, the tenant does not exercise exclusive control, the third party has its registered office there, and the landlord’s permission is not shown, the tenant is liable for eviction for parting with possession.

issues.legal_issue: Additional evidence on appeal should not be admitted when it could have been obtained and produced in the courts below and no satisfactory explanation is given for the failure to do so.
material_facts: The respondent sought permission under Order 41 Rule 27 of the Code of Civil Procedure to produce club reports, balance sheets and auditor’s reports to support a claim that the club was liable to pay rent.
The documents existed during the proceedings in the courts below and could have been obtained and filed before the trial court, the appellate court or the High Court.
The respondent offered no satisfactory explanation for not producing the documents earlier.
issues.conclusion: The application to produce the documents as additional evidence was dismissed because there was no justification for their admission at that stage.
issues.legal_principle: Order 41 Rule 27 of the Code of Civil Procedure permits additional evidence in an appeal only where its requirements justify admission. The Court found no justification where the documents could have been obtained and produced in the courts below and no satisfactory explanation was offered for the failure to do so.

predicates.appeal_seeking_additional_evidence: A party to an appeal asks to introduce additional documents as evidence.
predicates.documents_were_earlier_obtainable: The documents could have been obtained and produced during proceedings in the courts below.
predicates.no_satisfactory_explanation_for_earlier_: The party gives no satisfactory explanation for failing to produce the documents earlier.

issues.definition: When a party seeks additional evidence on appeal, the documents were obtainable earlier, and the party gives no satisfactory explanation for the omission, the application is denied.
